evidence_type: Bounded read-only Android RFCOMM connection attempt under the owner's authorized ADB shell identity; no status request was sent and no setter was invoked
device: Nothing A001 (Galaga / GalagaIND), Android 16, Build BP2A.250605.031.A3
headset: realme TechLife Studio H1, bonded and active A2DP/LDAC device; address redacted here
authorization: Owner stated the devices were connected and not in use and approved proceeding
method: A reflection-only Java runner dexed with D8 and launched via app_process as ADB shell (uid 2000, BLUETOOTH_PRIVILEGED and BLUETOOTH_CONNECT granted). No app installed or modified.

attempts.transport: BluetoothDevice.createRfcommSocket(1) using the documented RFCOMM channel

constraints: No blind channel or opcode sweep was performed after the two documented variants failed.
No pairing, bonding, disassociation, firmware or headset command was attempted.
No Android companion association was created for our app.
The temporary dex was removed from /data/local/tmp after the attempt.

interpretation.conclusion: On this Android 16 phone, under the ADB shell identity, neither documented RFCOMM route opened a socket while the H1 was connected over A2DP. No H1 status bytes were observed on Android, so this does not corroborate or contradict the earlier Windows status result.
unknown_causes: A2DP/SPP contention on the connected headset
Android stack restrictions on shell-initiated RFCOMM
H1 not advertising the SPP UUID via SDP on this Android build
Device state at the moment of the attempt
not_proven: That the H1 lacks an Android-accessible RFCOMM endpoint
That our uncompiled H1Link can or cannot connect

follow_up: Retest from a real installed app with the user-approved companion association and a foreground UI, using one explicit refresh() and bounded logging. Do not infer success from the shell negative.
